reviews.review: It's space ninjas, does more need to be said? Fluid combat with an emphasis on awesome acrobatics and hyper-cool weaponry. More than a dozen different warframes, each with their own play style, await you within. So what are you waiting for? Grab your space katana and go cut up some nasties!

Ok,

Pros:

Fast paced shooting mechanics, decent sword mechanics. Good mobility, customization not that good but workable. Teamwork, can still play solo however. And a stealth and free-run mechanic. Nvidia graphics and Physics! 

Cons:

You will NEVER get into PvP becuase of "Your inventory ### doesn't meet the requirements." Unfair, if not almost cheating AI. Cash store always dangled in front of your face. When the game adds a new playable Warframe, it feels like "YOU MUST PAY." in order to play it.  Feels unrewarding. Buggy beyond beleif, but that's because its an MMO. Near impossible to join a guild/clan. Notorius time waster. Lotus voice.


Overall: 

I enjoyed this game for a few days, but between DRM, lack of commmunication with other players, and cash store ads. I reached my Pain; enjoyment thresh hold.  It just seems like a time waster, and you never feel like you accomplish anything, unless you sink in $$$ of course. If you need to waste a few hours go ahead, but it just felt to as if there was no point to doing ALL of the same repeating missions OVER AND OVER again. It's up to you.

I hated Warframe for years. I didn't like how mindless the combat was. I didn't like how grindy the process of earning anything was. I didn't like how every weapon did the same thing but just looked different. 

But all that changed in 2016. Warframe's balance shifted from a World of Warcraft "Nerf everything" style to a DotA "Everything is OP in it's own way" method, and it's glorious. 

GAMEPLAY:
-Weapons are finally fun to level and collecting a vast armory is an absolute joy.
-Missions are no longer pointless kill-5-magical-pig grinds and are more like choose your own adventures. Very Killing Floor / Payday-esque, except SPACE NINJAS.
-Movement isn't restricted to console-like loot hallways and reminds me more of Tribes than I'd like to admit. 
-You can play the game like Elder Scrolls and ignore the "main quests" and story completely to just do alerts. I didn't start doing quests until I was 600+ hours in.
-Every 3 months new Prime parts (Arcana-esque cosmetics with minor perks) are released and available for 140$ (!!!!) but DE allows you to craft them in game for free with a little bit of effort. I've done this every time, for free, without having to spend a dime on the game. 
-Nothing requires a team, you can solo the entire game as far as I'm aware. It's as MMO as you want it to be.
-Rocket League-esque Lunaro mode.
-Pokemon Snap quests (I'm not joking, these devs are awesome.)
-Tamigachi pets which can join you in combat or simply dig up loot. Space dogs, floating robot eyes and soon magic space cats to tame and breed.
-Full PhysX combat and gore combined with abilities identical to jedi force powers makes fighting fun and interesting. I love throwing people off cliffs or slicing them in half. 
-Warframes are like Heroes/Champs and have their own role/playstyle. Vauban plants traps, Ash's ultimate is identical to Omnislash and Ember throws fireballs. Combat for spellcasters is very much like Skyrim (free targeting / throwing nukes) and City of Heroes (press 3 to freeze everyone around you, collect loot to restore mana quickly) Healers heal through combat and not passive beam nonsense like every other game these days.
-Everything is modular/customizable 
Crazy things you can do: 
Combine different elemental enchantments on your weapon to make a new one.
Stack crit% well over 100% so every hit is a critical. Your criticals can crit red numbers.
Strap tons of +damage % to a slow-swinging axe and cleave everything in half in one click.
Stack lots of +% Range and nuke an entire room or blink across the map.
-Gameplay scales well into "End game" depending on your commitment. It's a PVE game, so how much you commit is up to you, but the ability to buy, sell and trade "Primed Mods" means you are never done if you want to squeeze out an extra % of damage. (Primed Pressure Point costs a lot, but if you invest in it the damage scales past normal Pressure Point you get for free.)
Free versions are practically as good as Primed, but the option to min-max to all hell are available for hardcore folks.
-EXP is based on how much of the game you've experienced meaning it's impossible to find noobs at high levels. Levels are a reliable way to gauge how invested a player is and how knowledgable they are at the game. I LOVE THIS SYSTEM because it's the OPPOSITE of modern MMO's are designed - The game does not START at END-GAME. 
To increase your level you gain "mastery" which is given when you use/level a new weapon, frame or item to level 30. Very Planetside 1-esque and means you're always playing with new tools you'd normally never even consider - Nunchucks, Bows, Crossbows, Electric Whips, Dual swords, a bladed staff... Grab the blueprints for in-game money and craft 'em all. Then go adventure until they're level 30, sell the item OR craft it into something else (Craft 2 pistols together to make the Akimbo version, or turn a katana into a two handed blade of death, combine two assault rifles into a pistol-slot akimbo item. It's hilarious and fun, Love these devs.) 


ECONOMY: 
-Free to play game where you can actually get premium currency by just playing: Doing missions and Void towers nets you random Prime parts which you can sell to other players for real money currency. It's very easy to make a lot of Premium Currency without spending a dime. Made 100p off one piece last night. 
-Logging in has daily rewards, including 75% off (!!!) currency coupons - Buy 200$ worth of platinum for 50$ and get 600+ hours out of Warframe instead of 6 hours in some steam sale game for the same price. 
-Devs give you the option to buy anything for crazy high prices (in platinum) BUT Player-set prices are ROCK BOTTOM. You can buy Saryn Prime's pieces (3 pieces + blueprint to craft them together) for 120 platinum(1-3$ usd) TOTAL (1 trade with 1 player), or 10p per piece. (4 trades with 4 players) Sites like [url=https://warframe.market/]warframe.market[/url] make this an absolute breeze but if you knew how to use Trade Chat in World of Warcraft it's the same thing. A little bit of effort saves you 80$ usd. 
-The option to pay the devs (support the game) at much higher prices is available if you choose to not interact with people at all / instant grantification 
-Everything in the game is crafted on your ship except for exclusive cosmetics, but every mmo/f2p has those.
-Healthy economy with people buying and selling all the time at reasonable prices, very competitive market model means you can barter for better prices if you know what you're doing. Or just pay the price listed for hastle-free trades.
-Boosters increase amount gained, not drop numbers, thus rare resources stay rare and no pay2win (It's a PVE game anyway, so it's not a big deal.)
-Pay for Convienece model makes casual play tolerable (Crafting takes 12 hours, so queue up some things and go to bed/work/school/etc) Eve-like offline progress. Can pay to rush things (3 day uber items are 50p which is 50cents-1$ which is reasonable when people spend 2.50$ on crate keys in other games and get 0.03$ items for it without blinking an eye)
-It's entirely possible to collect all of the "Prime" versions of warframes for under 40$ usd, most only costing 1-5$ and Ember Prime currently rocking a whooping 20-30ish in platinum. (I paid 800p for the set but most of the prices I see are 1200-1500p) Basically you can get all the premium stuff just playing the game, selling parts to other players and then buying the parts you need from other players in the Ironforge-like locations (hub cities) Or do what I did and get a 75% off coupon, buy some currency and grab all the premium gear for a fraction of it. I've only bought currency one ever and It's all I needed - check out my screenshots.
-Devs support Humble Bundle often with FREE boosters, skins, weapons,etc (Donate 0.01 for promo keys) Or 1$ (The week-long boosters during E3)
-Anniversary events award any player who finished the tutorial with incredible gear. Dual swords that use a discontinued (Vaulted) Prime Sword model? Hell yes.

2016 Warframe pretty much requires you to use the wiki as nothing is explained in game, so if you're looking for an adventure you can go in blind and just figure it out as you go - most people will use a wiki or ask friends though. Next update (summer 2016 is expected) will streamline the map and make the new player experience less of a chore to research.

Just playing the game you'll eventually run into developers also playing the game, which is an awesome thing to see. Met them at Pax East - Literally the coolest people at the convention and super friendly and fun. They're the reason I gave Warframe another try and I'm so glad I did, so the least I can do is write a legit review detailing the game if you haven't tried it yet.
